title: I-27 Numbering Act of 2023
official_summary:
I–27 Numbering Act of 2023

This act designates the future interstate highway system portions of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor within the states of Texas and New Mexico as Interstate Route I–27.

In Texas, from Sterling City to Lamesa, U.S. Route 87 is designated as Interstate Route I–27E and Texas Routes 158 and 349 via I–20 are designated as Interstate Route I–27W. The act also excludes one portion of the Texas and New Mexico corridor; U.S. Route 287 from Dumas, Texas to the border between Texas and Oklahoma is designated as Interstate Route I–127N.

summary.headline: New law assigns Interstate 27 route numbers to future interstate sections of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor in Texas and New Mexico.
summary.what_it_does: The law names the future interstate highway parts of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor in Texas and New Mexico as Interstate 27 (I-27). Between Sterling City and Lamesa, Texas, the route splits: U.S. Route 87 becomes I-27E, and Texas Routes 158 and 349 (by way of I-20) become I-27W. One section, U.S. Route 287 from Dumas, Texas, to the Oklahoma border, is instead numbered I-127N.

who_it_affects.group: Drivers and truckers who travel these routes in Texas and New Mexico
who_it_affects.how: Roads they use will carry new interstate route numbers once those sections become part of the interstate system.

who_it_affects.group: Texas and New Mexico state transportation agencies
who_it_affects.how: They will use the new I-27, I-27E, I-27W, and I-127N numbers for these corridor sections.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law March 22, 2024. The summary does not give a separate start date, and the numbers apply to corridor sections as they become part of the interstate system.
